question: According to the Indian calendar, Hemanta season falls in which months?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Margashirsha-Pausa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National (Saka) Calendar divides the year into six seasons (Ritus), each spanning two lunar months. (हेमंत ऋतु — मार्गशीर्ष-पौष)

 

• Hemanta (winter/pre-winter) season corresponds to the months of Margashirsha and Pausa, roughly mid-November to mid-January.

 

• The six seasons in order are: Vasanta (Chaitra-Vaisakha), Grishma (Jyaistha-Asadha), Varsha (Sravana-Bhadra), Sarad (Asvina-Kartika), Hemanta (Margashirsha-Pausa), and Sisira (Magha-Phalguna).

 

• This six-season classification is rooted in ancient Indian tradition and is still used in the Indian national civil calendar, adopted officially on 22 March 1957.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Saka calendar begins on 1 Chaitra (usually 22 March, or 21 March in leap years) and its year count started from 78 CE.

 

• The six-season cycle also appears extensively in classical Sanskrit literature, such as Kalidasa's Ritusamhara.

 

NOTE

 

• Sravana-Bhadra (Option 1): These months correspond to the Varsha (monsoon) season, not Hemanta.

 

• Chaitra-Vaisakha (Option 2): These months correspond to the Vasanta (spring) season.

 

• Jyaistha-Asadha (Option 3): These months correspond to the Grishma (summer) season.

question: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alkynes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among hydrocarbons with a comparable number of carbon atoms, alkynes (containing a carbon-carbon triple bond) generally have the highest boiling points. (एल्काइन — उच्चतम क्वथनांक)

 

• This is because the linear geometry and greater electron density/polarizability of the triple bond lead to stronger intermolecular (van der Waals) forces compared to alkenes (double bond) and alkanes (single bond).

 

• The general trend in boiling point for hydrocarbons with the same carbon count is: Alkynes > Alkenes > Alkanes.

 

• Free carbon dioxide is a small, non-polar, linear molecule that sublimes at about -78.5°C at atmospheric pressure, giving it a much lower boiling/sublimation point than hydrocarbon chains of comparable size.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons (single bonds only); alkenes and alkynes are unsaturated, containing double and triple bonds respectively.

 

• Boiling points of hydrocarbons generally increase with molecular weight/chain length within each homologous series.

 

NOTE

 

• Alkenes (Option 1): Contain a C=C double bond; their boiling point is intermediate between alkanes and alkynes.

 

• Alkanes (Option 2): Contain only single bonds and have the lowest boiling points among the three hydrocarbon classes.

 

• Free carbon dioxide (Option 3): A small linear molecule that sublimes at a very low temperature, well below hydrocarbon boiling points.

question: When was the National Urban Health Mission approved by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2013.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Urban Health Mission (NUHM) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 1 May 2013. (राष्ट्रीय शहरी स्वास्थ्य मिशन — 2013)

 

• NUHM was launched as a sub-mission of the National Health Mission (NHM), the other sub-mission being the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM).

 

• Its primary aim is to meet the health needs of the urban population, especially the urban poor and vulnerable sections, by improving access to quality primary healthcare through a revamped public health system.

 

• NUHM covers all state capitals, district headquarters, and cities/towns with a population of more than 50,000 (as per the 2011 Census).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Health Mission (NHM) was launched in 2013 by merging NRHM (launched in 2005) and the newly created NUHM under one umbrella.

 

• Key components of NUHM include Urban Primary Health Centres (UPHCs), ASHA workers in urban slums, and Mahila Arogya Samitis.

 

NOTE

 

• 2014, 2015, 2012 (Options 1, 2 and 3): These are incorrect; NUHM's Cabinet approval date was 2013, not any of these years.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which group of states of India has the highest population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state with a population of about 19.98 crore, and Maharashtra is the second-most populous with about 11.24 crore. (जनगणना 2011 — उत्तर प्रदेश और महाराष्ट्र)

 

• Together, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra form the group with the highest combined population among the options given.

 

• Bihar ranks third (about 10.4 crore) in population as per Census 2011, ahead of West Bengal.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur are both small north-eastern states with comparatively very low populations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, India's total population was about 121.08 crore, making it the second most populous country in the world at the time (after China).

 

• The top five most populous states in 2011 were: Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal, and Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur (Option 2): Both are small north-eastern states with populations far below the national leaders.

 

• Maharashtra and Bihar (Option 3): Individually populous, but this pair's combined population is lower than Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra's.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Bihar (Option 4): Also a large combined population, but lower than the Uttar Pradesh-Maharashtra combination since Maharashtra's population exceeds Bihar's.

question: Which of the following cyclones did NOT hit India during the years 2021-2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Julia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cyclone Julia did not hit India — it was a tropical storm that affected Nicaragua and Central America in the Caribbean/Atlantic basin in October 2022, unrelated to the North Indian Ocean. (चक्रवात जूलिया — भारत में नहीं आया)

 

• Cyclone Yaas (May 2021) made landfall on the Odisha coast, causing widespread damage in Odisha and West Bengal.

 

• Cyclone Tauktae (May 2021) was a very severe cyclonic storm that struck the west coast of India, particularly Gujarat.

 

• Cyclone Gulab (September 2021) made landfall near the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cyclones in the North Indian Ocean are named alternately by countries in the region under a WMO/ESCAP scheme; India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and others contribute names.

 

• Yaas was named by India, Tauktae by Myanmar, and Gulab by Pakistan.

 

NOTE

 

• Yaas (Option 1): A cyclone that struck Odisha's coast in May 2021.

 

• Tauktae (Option 3): A cyclone that struck India's west coast (Gujarat) in May 2021.

 

• Gulab (Option 4): A cyclone that struck the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast in September 2021.

question: Identify the function of lipase in the process of digestion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Breaking down emulsified fats.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lipase is a digestive enzyme that breaks down emulsified fats (triglycerides) into fatty acids and glycerol. (लाइपेज़ — वसा का पाचन)

 

• Fats are first emulsified by bile (secreted by the liver, stored in the gallbladder), which breaks large fat globules into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase to act on.

 

• Pancreatic lipase is the primary lipase involved and acts in the small intestine (duodenum); smaller amounts of lipase are also secreted in saliva and gastric juice.

 

• The fatty acids and glycerol produced are then absorbed by the intestinal lining and used by the body for energy storage, cell membrane formation, etc.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amylase digests carbohydrates (starch) into simpler sugars, while proteases (e.g., trypsin, pepsin) digest proteins into amino acids/peptides.

 

• The pancreas secretes a mix of enzymes — amylase, lipase, and proteases — into the small intestine as part of pancreatic juice.

 

NOTE

 

• Breaking down roughage (Option 1): Roughage (dietary fibre) is largely indigestible by human enzymes and is not broken down by lipase.

 

• Secreting intestinal fluids (Option 3): This is the function of intestinal glands, not lipase.

 

• Digesting proteins (Option 4): This is the function of proteolytic enzymes such as pepsin and trypsin, not lipase.

question: Who among the following Kathak dancers of India founded the KADAMB Centre for Dance in 1964?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumudini Lakhia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kumudini Lakhia, an eminent Kathak dancer and choreographer, founded the Kadamb Centre for Dance and Music in Ahmedabad in 1964. (कदंब नृत्य केंद्र — कुमुदिनी लाखिया)

 

• She is known for modernising Kathak by introducing abstract, minimalist choreography while retaining its classical grammar.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri (1987) and Padma Bhushan (2010) for her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

• Her notable disciples trained at Kadamb include Aditi Mangaldas and Daksha Sheth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating primarily in North India, with the Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras gharanas.

 

• Kumudini Lakhia received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1982 for her contribution to Kathak.

 

NOTE

 

• Shovana Narayan (Option 1): A well-known Kathak exponent trained under Pandit Birju Maharaj, but she did not found Kadamb.

 

• Sitara Devi (Option 2): A legendary Kathak dancer of the Banaras gharana, known as "Nritya Samragini"; she did not found Kadamb.

 

• Rohini Bhate (Option 3): A noted Kathak dancer and guru from Maharashtra, but not the founder of Kadamb.

question:
Which of the following is the correct match of the column-A with column-B?

Column-A (Name of Disease) | Column-B (Affected Organs)

i. Alzheimer's diseases | a. Salivary glands

ii. Diphtheria | b. Reproductive tract

iii. Gonorrhoea | c. Brain

iv. Mumps | d. Nose and throat
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that primarily affects the brain, causing memory loss and cognitive decline (i-c). (अल्जाइमर रोग — मस्तिष्क)

 

• Diphtheria is a bacterial infection (caused by *Corynebacterium diphtheriae*) that primarily affects the nose and throat, forming a grey membrane in the throat (ii-d).

 

• Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection (caused by *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*) that primarily affects the reproductive tract (iii-b).

 

• Mumps is a viral infection that primarily affects the salivary glands (especially the parotid glands), causing swelling (iv-a).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diphtheria and Mumps are both preventable through vaccination — Diphtheria via the DPT vaccine and Mumps via the MMR vaccine.

 

• Alzheimer's disease is named after German psychiatrist Alois Alzheimer, who first described it in 1906.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-c, ii-a, iii-b, iv-d): Incorrectly swaps the organs affected by Diphtheria and Mumps.

 

• Option 2 (i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a): Incorrectly swaps the organs affected by Alzheimer's disease and Diphtheria.

 

• Option 3 (i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b): Incorrectly swaps the organs affected by Gonorrhoea and Mumps.

question: Which of the following is NOT an initiative by the government for development of the microfinance sector in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched in 2014, is a broad financial inclusion scheme aimed at ensuring access to basic banking (savings/deposit accounts) for every household — it is not a microfinance-specific initiative. (प्रधानमंत्री जन धन योजना — वित्तीय समावेशन)

 

• The E-Shakti Initiative, launched by NABARD, is a project to digitise Self-Help Group (SHG) accounts, directly supporting microfinance through SHGs.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), launched in 2015, provides collateral-free micro-loans (up to ₹10 lakh) to small/micro enterprises through MUDRA — a core microfinance-support initiative.

 

• The India Microfinance Equity Fund, set up by SIDBI, provides equity/quasi-equity support to smaller microfinance institutions (MFIs) to help them meet capital adequacy norms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) plays a key role in promoting microfinance in India through the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme.

 

• MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) categorises loans into Shishu, Kishor, and Tarun based on the loan amount.

 

NOTE

 

• E-Shakti Initiative (Option 2): A NABARD initiative to digitise SHG bookkeeping, directly aiding microfinance delivery.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (Option 3): A dedicated micro-credit scheme for small businesses, core to India's microfinance ecosystem.

 

• India Micro Finance Equity Fund (Option 4): A SIDBI fund specifically created to strengthen the equity base of microfinance institutions.

question: The maximum distance covered in a marathon is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42.195 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The standard/official distance of a marathon race is 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards). (मैराथन दौड़ — 42.195 किमी)

 

• This distance was standardised at the 1908 London Olympics and formally adopted by the IAAF (now World Athletics) in 1921.

 

• The event commemorates the legendary run of the Greek soldier Pheidippides from the town of Marathon to Athens.

 

• A half marathon covers half this distance, i.e., 21.0975 km.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The marathon has been part of the Olympic Games athletics programme since the first modern Olympics in 1896 in Athens.

 

• The current men's marathon world record is held by Kelvin Kiptum of Kenya.

 

NOTE

 

• 40 km, 42.5 km, 41.5 km (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are all incorrect; none matches the internationally standardised marathon distance of 42.195 km.

question: Elphinstone was the Governor of which province of India during 1819-27?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mountstuart Elphinstone served as the Governor of Bombay Presidency from 1819 to 1827. (माउंटस्टुअर्ट एल्फिन्स्टन — बॉम्बे के गवर्नर)

 

• He took charge of the Bombay Presidency shortly after the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818), in which he played a key administrative role.

 

• As governor, he undertook major administrative reforms, including codifying regulations into the "Elphinstone Code", and promoted education, founding institutions that later became Elphinstone College, Mumbai.

 

• He earlier served as the British Resident at the court of the Peshwa in Pune.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Elphinstone declined the offer to become Governor-General of India, preferring to retire from active service.

 

• Elphinstone College (established 1856, Mumbai) and Elphinstone Road (now Prabhadevi) railway station in Mumbai are named after him.

 

NOTE

 

• North West Frontier Province (Option 1): Elphinstone is known for an earlier mission to Kabul (1808-09), but he was not its governor.

 

• Madras (Option 2): He did not serve as Governor of Madras.

 

• Bengal (Option 3): He did not serve as Governor of Bengal.

question: India won the Thomas Cup in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its maiden Thomas Cup title in 2022, defeating 14-time champions Indonesia 3-0 in the final held in Bangkok, Thailand. (थॉमस कप 2022 — भारत)

 

• The Indian team was led by Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth, HS Prannoy, and the doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty.

 

• The Thomas Cup is the premier international men's team badminton championship, organised by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).

 

• This win ended a long wait, as India had never previously won the title in the tournament's history (first held in 1949).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Uber Cup is the equivalent women's team championship in badminton.

 

• India successfully defended its Thomas Cup title in 2024, held in Chengdu, China.

 

NOTE

 

• 2018, 2019, 2020 (Options 1, 2 and 4): India did not win the Thomas Cup in any of these years; its historic maiden win came only in 2022.

question: Who was the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The second session of the Indian National Congress was held in Calcutta in December 1886, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji. (दादाभाई नौरोजी — दूसरा कांग्रेस अधिवेशन)

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the "Grand Old Man of India", later presided over the Congress two more times — in 1893 (Lahore) and 1906 (Calcutta).

 

• He was also the author of the influential "Drain of Wealth" theory, articulated in his book *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*.

 

• He was the first Indian to become a member of the British House of Commons (elected in 1892).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first session of the INC was held in Bombay in December 1885, presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee.

 

• The INC was founded in 1885 with Allan Octavian Hume as a key organiser.

 

NOTE

 

• Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (Option 2): Presided over the first INC session (Bombay, 1885), not the second.

 

• Pherozeshah Mehta (Option 3): Presided over the third INC session (Madras, 1887), not the second.

 

• George Yule (Option 4): Presided over the INC session in 1888 (Allahabad); he was the first Englishman/Briton to preside over the Congress, but not at the second session.

question: Who among the following was a Padma Bhushan awardee, legendary Bharatanatyam exponent, theosophist and founder of the Kalakshetra Dance School?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was a legendary Bharatanatyam dancer, theosophist, and animal rights activist who founded Kalakshetra in Chennai (then Madras) in 1936. (कलाक्षेत्र — रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल)

 

• She is credited with reviving and reforming Bharatanatyam, removing certain associations with the Devadasi system and giving it a respectable, codified stage form.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 1956 for her contribution to Indian classical dance and culture.

 

• She was closely associated with the Theosophical Society, headquartered in Adyar, Chennai, and was married to theosophist George Arundale.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was also nominated to the Rajya Sabha and was a founding member of animal welfare organisations, notably drafting India's early animal welfare legislation.

 

• She was offered the post of President of India in 1977 (by the Janata Party) but declined it.

 

NOTE

 

• Sonal Mansingh (Option 1): A renowned Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer, Padma Vibhushan awardee, but not the founder of Kalakshetra.

 

• Saroja Vaidyanathan (Option 2): A well-known Bharatanatyam guru who founded the Ganesa Natyalaya, not Kalakshetra.

 

• Mallika Sarabhai (Option 4): A noted Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, daughter of Vikram Sarabhai, but not the founder of Kalakshetra.

question: M S Subbulakshmi, a legend in India is known for which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M. S. Subbulakshmi was a legendary Carnatic classical vocalist, widely regarded as one of the greatest singers of Indian classical music. (एम एस सुब्बुलक्ष्मी — कर्नाटक संगीत)

 

• She was the first musician ever to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 1998.

 

• She was also honoured with the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1974), becoming the first Indian musician to receive it, and the Padma Vibhushan (1975).

 

• Her rendition of "Kurai Onrum Illai" and the Venkatesa Suprabhatam are iconic and widely popular across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• M. S. Subbulakshmi sang at the United Nations General Assembly in 1966, one of the few Indian classical musicians to do so.

 

• Carnatic music is the classical music tradition of South India, as distinct from Hindustani music, the classical tradition of North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghazal music (Option 1): A form of Urdu/Persian poetic musical expression; M. S. Subbulakshmi was not primarily known for ghazals.

 

• Sufi devotional music (Option 2): Associated with Sufi saints and qawwali traditions, not her area of expertise.

 

• Hindustani music (Option 3): The North Indian classical tradition; M. S. Subbulakshmi was a Carnatic (South Indian) musician, not a Hindustani one.

question:
Which of the following is a negative effect of Green Revolution in India?

(i) Depletion of groundwater table

(ii) Deterioration in the quality of soil

(iii) Increased input cost
solution_text:
The correct answer is (i), (ii) and (iii).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution (starting mid-1960s, associated with M. S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug) significantly boosted foodgrain production but also caused several negative environmental and economic effects. (हरित क्रांति — नकारात्मक प्रभाव)

 

• Depletion of groundwater table (i): Excessive reliance on tube-well irrigation for water-intensive HYV crops (like wheat and rice) led to over-extraction and falling water tables, especially in Punjab and Haryana.

 

• Deterioration in soil quality (ii): Intensive monocropping and excessive use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides degraded soil fertility, caused salinity/waterlogging, and reduced micronutrient content over time.

 

• Increased input cost (iii): Green Revolution technology required costly inputs — HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation, and machinery — raising the cost of cultivation for farmers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution was largely concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh, leading to regional imbalances in agricultural development.

 

• It also contributed to income disparities between large and small farmers, as large farmers could better afford the new inputs.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because each of them omits one or more of the genuine negative effects — all three listed statements (groundwater depletion, soil deterioration, and increased input cost) are correct.

question: Under the Rail Kaushal Vikas Yojana launched in September 2021, the Government of India has proposed to impart training to a total of 50,000 candidates over a ______-year period.
solution_text:
The correct answer is three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rail Kaushal Vikas Yojana (RKVY) was launched in September 2021 by the Indian Railways, under the umbrella of the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana. (रेल कौशल विकास योजना — तीन वर्ष)

 

• Under the scheme, the government aims to train 50,000 youth (candidates) across 75 Railway Training Institutes over a period of three years.

 

• Training is initially imparted in four trades: Electrician, Welder, Machinist, and Fitter, and is free of cost for eligible candidates aged 18-35 years.

 

• The objective is skill development for candidates (10th pass), enhancing their employability, though it does not guarantee a job with Indian Railways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• RKVY is part of the Indian Railways' broader corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative for youth skill development.

 

• Successful candidates receive a certificate upon completion of the training and assessment.

 

NOTE

 

• Four, two, five (Options 1, 2 and 3): These are incorrect; the officially proposed training period under RKVY is three years, not four, two, or five.

question:
Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

(A): An object slips less on a rough surface than a smooth surface.

(R): When a surface is rough, frictional force increases.
option_1: Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
option_2: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
option_3: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.
option_4: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true: An object indeed slips less on a rough surface than on a smooth surface — this is a well-established observation in mechanics. (घर्षण बल — खुरदरी सतह)

 

• Reason (R) is true: A rougher surface has a higher coefficient of friction, which increases the frictional force resisting relative motion between the surfaces.

 

• R correctly explains A: Since friction is the force that opposes sliding, a higher frictional force on a rough surface directly causes less slipping, making R the correct explanation for A.

 

• Friction arises due to the microscopic interlocking of surface irregularities; rougher surfaces have more such irregularities, increasing resistance to sliding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The force of friction is given by f = μN, where μ is the coefficient of friction (higher for rougher surfaces) and N is the normal reaction force.

 

• Lubricants are used to reduce friction by smoothing the effective contact between surfaces.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect because Reason (R) is also true, not false.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect because R does correctly explain A — increased friction on a rough surface is precisely why the object slips less.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect because Assertion (A) is true, not false — objects genuinely slip less on rough surfaces.

question: On 1 February 2021, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman informed that ______ and ______ will be merged under the umbrella of Mission POSHAN 2.0.
option_1: Supplementary Health Programme; National health Mission
option_2: Supplementary Nutrition Programme; National Health Mission
option_3: Supplementary Nutrition Programme; National Nutrition Mission
option_4: Supplementary Health Programme; National Nutrition Mission
solution_text:
The correct answer is Supplementary Nutrition Programme; National Nutrition Mission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• While presenting the Union Budget 2021-22 on 1 February 2021, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that the Supplementary Nutrition Programme and the Poshan Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission) would be merged and launched as Mission POSHAN 2.0. (मिशन पोषण 2.0 — पोषण अभियान)

 

• POSHAN Abhiyaan was originally launched in 2018 as India's flagship programme to improve nutritional outcomes for children, adolescent girls, pregnant women, and lactating mothers, and was also referred to as the National Nutrition Mission.

 

• Mission POSHAN 2.0 aims to strengthen nutritional content, delivery, outreach, and outcomes by adopting a strategic shift towards a life-cycle approach.

 

• The mission is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mission POSHAN 2.0 was later brought under the broader Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 umbrella, integrating Anganwadi infrastructure upgrades as well.

 

• The scheme focuses on addressing malnutrition, anaemia, low birth weight, and improving overall health indicators among women and children.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because they misidentify one or both of the merged programmes — the actual merger was of the Supplementary Nutrition Programme and the National Nutrition Mission (Poshan Abhiyaan), not the "Supplementary Health Programme" or "National Health Mission".

question: Who among the following was appointed as the chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Rituraj Awasthi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Rituraj Awasthi (retired Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court) was appointed as the Chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission of India in November 2022. (22वां विधि आयोग — रितुराज अवस्थी)

 

• The 22nd Law Commission of India was constituted for a period of three years from 21 February 2020, though the chairperson's position had remained vacant for some time before his appointment.

 

• The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory body constituted by the Government of India, tasked with legal reforms, reviewing and recommending changes to laws.

 

• It is reconstituted periodically and works closely with the Ministry of Law and Justice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Law Commission of independent India was constituted in 1955, chaired by then Attorney General M. C. Setalvad.

 

• The Law Commission submits reports on various legal issues, which the government may or may not act upon, as its recommendations are not binding.

 

NOTE

 

• Justice UU Lalit (Option 1): Served as the 49th Chief Justice of India; he was not the chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission.

 

• Justice VV Raman (Option 2) and Justice KT Shankaran (Option 3): Neither was appointed as chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission of India.

question:
Assume a situation where A has gone to a cinema hall with her friends to watch a movie. In the next seat she realises that it is her maid who is also watching the movie.

Now A asks her maid to leave the cinema hall.

In the above scenario, which of the following Article of the Constitution of India can provide relief to the maid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 15 of the Constitution of India prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. (अनुच्छेद 15 — भेदभाव निषेध)

 

• Article 15(2) specifically guarantees that no citizen shall, on these grounds, be subject to any disability, liability, restriction, or condition with regard to access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment — a cinema hall falls squarely within "places of public entertainment".

 

• In this scenario, A asking her maid — typically from a socially/economically disadvantaged background often correlated with caste — to leave a place of public entertainment amounts to discriminatory exclusion from a public space, attracting protection under Article 15(2).

 

• Article 15 is a Fundamental Right available against the State, but its principle of non-discrimination in access to public places is widely cited in such scenario-based questions to protect citizens from discriminatory exclusion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 15(3), (4), (5) and (6) allow the State to make special provisions for women, children, socially/educationally backward classes, SCs/STs, and economically weaker sections.

 

• Article 15 falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution, under the broader Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 16 (Option 1): Provides for equality of opportunity in matters of public employment, not relevant to a cinema hall scenario.

 

• Article 18 (Option 3): Deals with the abolition of titles (e.g., prohibiting the State from conferring titles other than military/academic distinctions), unrelated to this scenario.

 

• Article 17 (Option 4): Abolishes "untouchability" in any form; while related to caste discrimination, this scenario is about access to a public place and is more directly covered by Article 15(2).

question: Who among the following was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sukumar Sen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India, serving from 21 March 1950 to 19 December 1958. (सुकुमार सेन — प्रथम मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त)

 

• Under his leadership, the Election Commission of India conducted the first general elections of independent India in 1951-52, a massive logistical exercise given the country's size and largely illiterate electorate.

 

• He also oversaw the second general elections in 1957.

 

• Sukumar Sen was later awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1954 for his contribution to conducting India's first elections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution, responsible for administering elections in India.

 

• The Election Commission was originally a single-member body until it became a multi-member body in 1989 (later made permanent from 1993).

 

NOTE

 

• Dr. Nagendra Singh (Option 1): A distinguished jurist who later served as a judge and President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), not the first CEC.

 

• SP Sen Verma (Option 2): Served as a later Chief Election Commissioner of India (1958-1967), not the first.

 

• KVK Sundaram (Option 4): Served as a subsequent Chief Election Commissioner (1967-1972), not the first.

question: Which festival traces its origin to the Tibetan New Year and in Ladakh, it is celebrated every year at the end of the harvesting season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Losar festival.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Losar festival traces its origin to the Tibetan New Year and is celebrated in Ladakh at the end of the harvesting season, typically in December. (लोसर पर्व — लद्दाख)

 

• "Losar" literally means "new year" in Tibetan ("Lo" = year, "Sar" = new), and marks the beginning of the new year in the Tibetan lunar calendar.

 

• The festival is celebrated with traditional dances, prayers at monasteries, feasting, and cultural performances, especially by Buddhist communities in Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Losar celebrations in Ladakh typically begin about two months earlier than in Tibet, as it also coincides with the completion of the harvest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Losar is celebrated with variations across Tibetan Buddhist regions including Sikkim, Bhutan, and Nepal.

 

• Other Ladakhi festivals with monastic mask (Cham) dances include Hemis Festival, Losar, and Dosmoche.

 

NOTE

 

• Matho Nagrang (Option 2): A Ladakhi festival held at Matho Monastery featuring the famous oracle rituals, not linked to the Tibetan New Year harvest timing.

 

• Yuru Kabgyat (Option 3): A masked dance festival held at Hemis Monastery, celebrating Guru Padmasambhava's birth anniversary, not the Tibetan New Year.

 

• Dosmoche (Option 4): A monastic festival ('Festival of the Scapegoat') held in Leh and Diskit, distinct from the Losar/Tibetan New Year celebration.

question: Sabha and Ur, two kinds of village assemblies are referred to in which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Chola dynasty, local self-government was organised through village assemblies called "Sabha" and "Ur". (सभा और ऊर — चोल प्रशासन)

 

• The "Sabha" was an assembly of Brahmin (agrahara/brahmadeya) villages, functioning through specialised committees (variyams) for irrigation, justice, gardens, etc.

 

• The "Ur" was a more general village assembly, typically found in non-Brahmadeya (ordinary) villages, open to all adult male members/landholders of the village.

 

• Detailed information about the functioning of these assemblies comes from the famous Uttaramerur inscriptions (Chola period, Tamil Nadu), which describe the election process for the Sabha's committees.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Another Chola village institution was the "Nagaram", an assembly of merchants in trade centres/towns.

 

• The Chola administration is often cited as an early example of decentralised local self-government in Indian history.

 

NOTE

 

• Rashtrakuta (Option 2): Known for rock-cut architecture (e.g., Kailasa Temple, Ellora), not for the Sabha-Ur village assembly system.

 

• Gurjara Pratihara (Option 3): A north Indian dynasty, not associated with the Sabha-Ur system, which was specific to Chola (Tamil) village administration.

 

• Chalukya (Option 4): Known for temple architecture at Badami, Pattadakal, and Aihole; not associated with the Sabha-Ur assemblies.

question: Who among the following was defeated by Mauryan emperor Chandragupta Maurya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seleucus Nicator.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chandragupta Maurya, founder of the Mauryan Empire, defeated the Greek general Seleucus I Nicator in a war around 305 BCE. (सेल्यूकस निकेटर — चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य)

 

• Seleucus Nicator was one of Alexander the Great's generals who, after Alexander's death, established the Seleucid Empire covering large parts of Alexander's eastern conquests.

 

• Following his defeat, Seleucus signed a treaty (c. 303 BCE) with Chandragupta, ceding territories including parts of the trans-Indus region (including Gandhara) to the Mauryan Empire in exchange for 500 war elephants.

 

• The treaty was also sealed by a matrimonial alliance, and Seleucus sent Megasthenes as his ambassador to Chandragupta's court at Pataliputra, who later wrote the famous account "Indica".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE with the guidance of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the *Arthashastra*.

 

• The Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta's grandson Ashoka later became one of the largest empires in ancient Indian history.

 

NOTE

 

• Cassander (Option 1), Antigones/Antigonus (Option 3), and Ptolemy (Option 4): These were also generals (Diadochi) of Alexander the Great who divided his empire after his death, but it was specifically Seleucus Nicator, ruling the eastern territories bordering India, whom Chandragupta Maurya defeated in battle.
